Description: The 5NN01 port range (e.g. 50001, 50101, etc.) serves as the HTTPS-secured interface for SAP NetWeaver Java systems. These ports mirror the functionality of their 5NN00 HTTP counterparts but are encrypted via TLS. They're frequently used in production environments where encryption is enforced at the application layer or SSL is terminated at the edge (e.g., SAP Web Dispatcher or a load balancer).
Deployment Context: This HTTPS interface is common in hardened enterprise deployments of SAP Java stacks, such as Enterprise Portal (EP), Process Integration/Orchestration (PI/PO), and standalone Java Application Servers. It represents the secure entry point for administrators and users interacting with Java-based SAP services via the web.
Access Behavior: Ports in this range expose servlet-based Java web content over TLS. They may be directly exposed to users or administrators, or fronted by reverse proxies. Authentication is typically enforced via login forms, SAML2 flows, or SPNEGO mechanisms. Strong TLS configurations, hostname validation, and secure cookies are often implemented here.
Functional Capabilities: Exposed services typically include SAP Enterprise Portal (/irj/portal), NetWeaver Admin Console (/nwa), user management interfaces (/useradmin), Web Dynpro UIs, and integration APIs like SOAP, REST, and OData. These interfaces may also present SAML2 endpoints (/saml2/acs, /saml2/idp), client certificate prompts, and other advanced auth mechanisms.
Security Implications: Even though these ports are secured with TLS, their attack surface mirrors that of the HTTP interface. Misconfigurations, weak certificates, and verbose error messages can still pose risk. Improperly exposed services behind weak authentication may allow attackers to enumerate or access sensitive components. Failure to validate client certificates or hostname mismatches could degrade the intended security posture.
Detection Goals: This module intends to validate the presence and security posture of 5NN01 interfaces by probing known SAP endpoints (/nwa, /irj/, /wsnavigator), verifying certificate chains and hostname matches, and identifying Java version details from headers or content. It will also assess whether authentication is enforced and what mechanisms are in use.
Assessment Notes: If ports in the 5NN01 range are accessible and return valid SAP Java content, the host likely represents a hardened SAP NetWeaver Java instance. This may be the only exposed interface in strict environments, and should be closely monitored for abnormal access or misconfiguration. Ensure that certificate trust, auth policies, and exposed services are reviewed regularly.
